items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: Mike Lang, the pianist in L.A. who was helping me on some of this has sadly died.

ctx.x: Oh. Well Dick Hyman was my parents’ friend when we were back in New York. I knew him a little bit, Dick and Julia. But when I was living in northern California and my dad had passed away and I was going through a lot of CDs and re-issues in the garage to help my mom decide what to donate. And I came across this Fats Waller double CD called “Turn on the Heat.” And I just absolutely fell in love with it. My parents hadn’t played much stride music because it was too old fashioned for them. But I just loved it. I…

Waller sample. So Dick Hyman calls me up, and mind you I really didn’t know him at all except just vaguely. And he said, “All right,” he said, “you have to do a whole album of these stride piano pieces with your lyrics because who else is going to do it? And I like it because,” he said, “it’s like Lambert, Hendricks & Ross only the music is much older, even much older” he said, and I’ll plan it. But I don’t have time right now so find somebody else and then when it’s time” — and he began sending me all of these…
